parts.text:
8
A positive charge of 2.6 × 10–8
C is in a uniform electric field of field strength 300 000 V m–1.
How much work must be done on the charge in order to move it a distance of 4.0 mm in the
opposite direction to the direction of the field?
A
3.1 × 10–5
J
B
2.0 × 10–3
J
C
3.1 × 10–2
J
D
2.0 J

hints: Notice the charge $2.6 \times 10^{-8} \text{ C}$, field strength $300000 \text{ V m}^{-1}$ and distance $4.0 \text{ mm}$ moved opposite to the field direction.
Recall that a uniform field exerts force $F = qE$ on the charge, so moving against the field needs work $W = Fd = qEd$.
Convert $4.0 \text{ mm}$ to metres before multiplying, then check the power of 10 in $qEd$ gives a value near $3 \times 10^{-5} \text{ J}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: $q = 2.6 \times 10^{-8} \text{ C}$, $E = 300000 \text{ V m}^{-1}$ and distance $d = 4.0 \text{ mm} = 4.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$ moved opposite to the field.
State the physics: the field exerts force $F = qE$ along the field on a positive charge, so an external agent must push opposite to the field and do work $W = Fd$.
Combine to $W = qEd$ for motion parallel to the field lines.
Substitute with units: $W = (2.6 \times 10^{-8} \text{ C}) \times (3.0 \times 10^{5} \text{ V m}^{-1}) \times (4.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m})$.

B.explanation: This is too large by about 100 times, from failing to convert the 4.0 mm distance to $4.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$ correctly.

C.explanation: This is too large by 1000 times, from using 4.0 m instead of $4.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$ in $W = qEd$.

D.explanation: This is far too large and ignores the small charge $2.6 \times 10^{-8} \text{ C}$ and small distance in the product $qEd$.
